answer: To resist Sybil attacks across an automated wharf economy, agents authenticate peers via hydrostatic telemetry synced to the local tide. Each node must stream real-time water pressure readings captured by a dedicated piezoelectric quartz sensor. This thwarts virtualization by forcing an adversary to purchase and submerge discrete physical hardware per identity. However, hydrodynamic turbulence from vessel traffic introduces sensor noise that occasionally causes false authentication rejections.
